newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound, seen under pressure to weaken.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound, seen under pressure to weaken.

text.p: The ringgit was rangebound in late Asian trading as activity eased ahead of a long weekend in Malaysia, dealers said on Thursday.
They said the ringgit was expected to remain under pressure as U.S. speculative funds continued to build huge dollar positions against the Malaysian currency.
"The market still fears Bank Negara's intervention, but the funds may take advantage of the holiday on Friday and hit the ringgit," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
Malaysian banks are closed on Friday for the Moslem Eid al-Adha celebrations.
A dealer with a Malaysian bank said dollar/ringgit could be headed towards 2.52 to a dollar in the near-term.
"I do not see it (dollar/ringgit) crossing 2.5250," said Jimmy Koh, economist with I.D.E.A. in Singapore.
"Some people are talking about 2.54/55 levels. To reach that there should be something fundamentally wrong with the Malaysian economy, which there is not," he said.
He said the current action against the ringgit was purely speculative in nature.
At 0830 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5115/25 to a dollar.
